{
  "project_id": "P-UGA-IntegratedWaterMgmtDev",
  "risks": [
    {
      "risk_id": "R01",
      "description": "Ongoing conflict in South Sudan could worsen regional instability, driving further refugee influxes into Uganda and overstretching local public services and water natural resources.",
      "category": "external",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Coordinate closely with UNHCR and OPM through the Comprehensive Refugee Response Framework (CRRF) and invest in long-term sustainable water supply infrastructure in hosting districts.",
      "evidence": "The most critical risk to this outlook is regional instability, particularly from the ongoing conflict in South Sudan."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R02",
      "description": "Fiduciary and contract management weaknesses within MWE and NWSC could cause processing delays, multiple contract amendments, and significant time/cost overruns during civil works execution.",
      "category": "organizational",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Recruit dedicated procurement consultants, conduct capacity-building training on World Bank Procurement Regulations, and implement contract management plans for high-value contracts.",
      "evidence": "weakness resulted in multiple amendments during contract implementation resulting in cost and time overruns."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R03",
      "description": "Incomplete needs assessments and inadequate geotechnical studies prior to construction could lead to extensive design changes and variations during contract implementation.",
      "category": "technical",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Require outcome-based needs assessments and comprehensive geotechnical studies during the detailed engineering design phase prior to bidding.",
      "evidence": "incomplete needs assessments and inadequate attention to geotechnical studies leading to design changes/variations during implementation"
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R04",
      "description": "Limited capacity of local domestic contractors to execute complex water and sanitation projects could result in slow construction progress or sub-standard work quality.",
      "category": "external",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Package works contracts to match market capacity, encourage joint ventures and subconsultants, and utilize open international competitive procurement.",
      "evidence": "limited capacity of domestic contractors to conduct projects of this nature, complexity, and scope"
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R05",
      "description": "Incomplete operationalization of the project module within MWE's Integrated Financial Management System (IFMS) increases the risk of financial reporting errors and processing delays.",
      "category": "financial",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Fully operationalize the IFMS project module at MWE and maintain qualified financial management specialists within the Project Support Team.",
      "evidence": "the project module of the IFMS has not been fully operationalized at the MWE, which increases the risk of errors"
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R06",
      "description": "High climate variability, extreme temperatures, and intense rainfall events could cause severe water stress, flooding, and physical damage to raw water intakes and infrastructure.",
      "category": "environmental",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Integrate climate-resilient engineering designs, implement water source buffer protection, and conduct catchment management activities such as reforestation and soil conservation.",
      "evidence": "high climate variability and underdeveloped water resources infrastructure could result in significant water stress in areas of the country."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R07",
      "description": "An influx of construction labor into project host communities could trigger social conflicts, gender-based violence (GBV), sexual exploitation, and increased local transmission of STDs/HIV.",
      "category": "stakeholder",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Mandate worker codes of conduct, enforce labor influx management plans, maximize local workforce recruitment, and conduct mandatory GBV and HIV prevention training.",
      "evidence": "Long walks to water sources trigger serious social consequences, particularly GBV... Labor influx... potential GBV in Project areas."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R08",
      "description": "Land acquisition and pipeline rights-of-way alignment could cause physical and temporary economic displacement of local populations, leading to grievances and land disputes.",
      "category": "stakeholder",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Develop and implement site-specific Resettlement Action Plans (RAPs) prior to civil works, pay timely compensation, and establish functional local Grievance Redress Mechanisms.",
      "evidence": "road encroachment and potential works like plants, pump stations and storage tanks may have land acquisition implications and displacement"
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R09",
      "description": "Insufficient dry-season river flows in the Namatala River could undermine water supply reliability for Mbale Town while breaching required downstream environmental flow thresholds.",
      "category": "technical",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Conduct an Augmented Water Supply Study before construction to evaluate source impoundment, borehole supplementation, and alternative supply expansion options.",
      "evidence": "Namatala’s dry weather flows in some cases may not be sufficient to meet projected water demand and maintain an adequate EF."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R10",
      "description": "Regional Umbrella Water Authorities (UWAs) may experience initial operating losses in newly gazetted small towns due to low revenue collection rates and high initial operation costs.",
      "category": "financial",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Enforce cost-reflective tariffs with a minimum 25% margin, automate tariff adjustments, convert systems to low-cost solar power, and apply performance-based operator contracts.",
      "evidence": "Several of the systems will show operating losses in the first years of operation, but these losses will gradually decrease"
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R11",
      "description": "Improper operation of fecal sludge treatment facilities and wastewater lagoons could cause untreated effluent discharges, odor nuisance, water body contamination, and public health risks.",
      "category": "environmental",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Ensure facility designs include percolate treatment, construct watertight structures, provide operator training, and regularly monitor treated effluent quality against NEMA standards.",
      "evidence": "sludge management and wastewater effluent discharges that exceed standards; possible impacts on surface and/or ground water due to leakages"
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R12",
      "description": "Lack of structured coordination among humanitarian partners, local governments, and MWE in refugee districts could result in ill-sited boreholes and groundwater contamination risks.",
      "category": "organizational",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Establish formal multi-agency coordination mechanisms under MWE, OPM, and UNHCR to streamline water resource planning and borehole positioning.",
      "evidence": "lack of coordination resulted in boreholes being drilled too close to each other or too close to shallow pit latrines, risking contamination"
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R13",
      "description": "Prolonged internal administrative approval processes within government agencies could delay payments to vendors and contractors, slowing project execution.",
      "category": "schedule",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Establish an automated payment tracking system, enforce payment processing timelines, and strengthen internal audit and accounting workflows.",
      "evidence": "delays in paying vendors due to prolonged internal approval processes."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R14",
      "description": "Shifting refugee settlements from free emergency humanitarian water supply to paid user-tariff schemes under public utilities may meet social resistance or policy transition hurdles.",
      "category": "political_regulatory",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Collaborate with UNHCR and OPM on designing progressive refugee tariff policies linked to socio-economic support and conduct extensive community consultation.",
      "evidence": "refugees in settlements currently do not pay for water, the UNHCR and OPM are collaborating with the MWE on designing a new water tariff policy"
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R15",
      "description": "Over-reliance on diesel-powered mechanized pumping schemes exposes water schemes to high fuel costs, volatile operational expenses, and frequent service interruptions.",
      "category": "technical",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Prioritize solar-powered piped water systems and gravity-fed schemes during project design to minimize diesel reliance and lower running costs.",
      "evidence": "long-term savings on fuel and capital maintenance make solar pumping systems more cost-effective than alternative mechanized pumping systems."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R16",
      "description": "Turnover of qualified financial management and procurement staff within MWE and NWSC could impair institutional memory and slow project implementation.",
      "category": "organizational",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Maintain competitive staffing conditions, recruit dedicated PST specialists, and conduct regular hand-holding training sessions.",
      "evidence": "turnover of qualified and experienced staff is noticed."
    }
  ]
}

risks.description: Ongoing conflict in South Sudan could worsen regional instability, driving further refugee influxes into Uganda and overstretching local public services and water natural resources.
risks.mitigation: Coordinate closely with UNHCR and OPM through the Comprehensive Refugee Response Framework (CRRF) and invest in long-term sustainable water supply infrastructure in hosting districts.
risks.evidence: The most critical risk to this outlook is regional instability, particularly from the ongoing conflict in South Sudan.

risks.description: Fiduciary and contract management weaknesses within MWE and NWSC could cause processing delays, multiple contract amendments, and significant time/cost overruns during civil works execution.
risks.mitigation: Recruit dedicated procurement consultants, conduct capacity-building training on World Bank Procurement Regulations, and implement contract management plans for high-value contracts.
risks.evidence: weakness resulted in multiple amendments during contract implementation resulting in cost and time overruns.

risks.description: Incomplete needs assessments and inadequate geotechnical studies prior to construction could lead to extensive design changes and variations during contract implementation.
risks.mitigation: Require outcome-based needs assessments and comprehensive geotechnical studies during the detailed engineering design phase prior to bidding.
risks.evidence: incomplete needs assessments and inadequate attention to geotechnical studies leading to design changes/variations during implementation

risks.description: Limited capacity of local domestic contractors to execute complex water and sanitation projects could result in slow construction progress or sub-standard work quality.
risks.mitigation: Package works contracts to match market capacity, encourage joint ventures and subconsultants, and utilize open international competitive procurement.
risks.evidence: limited capacity of domestic contractors to conduct projects of this nature, complexity, and scope

risks.description: Incomplete operationalization of the project module within MWE's Integrated Financial Management System (IFMS) increases the risk of financial reporting errors and processing delays.
risks.mitigation: Fully operationalize the IFMS project module at MWE and maintain qualified financial management specialists within the Project Support Team.
risks.evidence: the project module of the IFMS has not been fully operationalized at the MWE, which increases the risk of errors

risks.description: High climate variability, extreme temperatures, and intense rainfall events could cause severe water stress, flooding, and physical damage to raw water intakes and infrastructure.
risks.mitigation: Integrate climate-resilient engineering designs, implement water source buffer protection, and conduct catchment management activities such as reforestation and soil conservation.
risks.evidence: high climate variability and underdeveloped water resources infrastructure could result in significant water stress in areas of the country.

risks.description: An influx of construction labor into project host communities could trigger social conflicts, gender-based violence (GBV), sexual exploitation, and increased local transmission of STDs/HIV.
risks.mitigation: Mandate worker codes of conduct, enforce labor influx management plans, maximize local workforce recruitment, and conduct mandatory GBV and HIV prevention training.
risks.evidence: Long walks to water sources trigger serious social consequences, particularly GBV... Labor influx... potential GBV in Project areas.

risks.description: Land acquisition and pipeline rights-of-way alignment could cause physical and temporary economic displacement of local populations, leading to grievances and land disputes.
risks.mitigation: Develop and implement site-specific Resettlement Action Plans (RAPs) prior to civil works, pay timely compensation, and establish functional local Grievance Redress Mechanisms.
risks.evidence: road encroachment and potential works like plants, pump stations and storage tanks may have land acquisition implications and displacement

risks.description: Insufficient dry-season river flows in the Namatala River could undermine water supply reliability for Mbale Town while breaching required downstream environmental flow thresholds.
risks.mitigation: Conduct an Augmented Water Supply Study before construction to evaluate source impoundment, borehole supplementation, and alternative supply expansion options.
risks.evidence: Namatala’s dry weather flows in some cases may not be sufficient to meet projected water demand and maintain an adequate EF.

risks.description: Regional Umbrella Water Authorities (UWAs) may experience initial operating losses in newly gazetted small towns due to low revenue collection rates and high initial operation costs.
risks.mitigation: Enforce cost-reflective tariffs with a minimum 25% margin, automate tariff adjustments, convert systems to low-cost solar power, and apply performance-based operator contracts.
risks.evidence: Several of the systems will show operating losses in the first years of operation, but these losses will gradually decrease

risks.description: Improper operation of fecal sludge treatment facilities and wastewater lagoons could cause untreated effluent discharges, odor nuisance, water body contamination, and public health risks.
risks.mitigation: Ensure facility designs include percolate treatment, construct watertight structures, provide operator training, and regularly monitor treated effluent quality against NEMA standards.
risks.evidence: sludge management and wastewater effluent discharges that exceed standards; possible impacts on surface and/or ground water due to leakages

risks.description: Lack of structured coordination among humanitarian partners, local governments, and MWE in refugee districts could result in ill-sited boreholes and groundwater contamination risks.
risks.mitigation: Establish formal multi-agency coordination mechanisms under MWE, OPM, and UNHCR to streamline water resource planning and borehole positioning.
risks.evidence: lack of coordination resulted in boreholes being drilled too close to each other or too close to shallow pit latrines, risking contamination

risks.description: Prolonged internal administrative approval processes within government agencies could delay payments to vendors and contractors, slowing project execution.
risks.mitigation: Establish an automated payment tracking system, enforce payment processing timelines, and strengthen internal audit and accounting workflows.
risks.evidence: delays in paying vendors due to prolonged internal approval processes.

risks.description: Shifting refugee settlements from free emergency humanitarian water supply to paid user-tariff schemes under public utilities may meet social resistance or policy transition hurdles.
risks.mitigation: Collaborate with UNHCR and OPM on designing progressive refugee tariff policies linked to socio-economic support and conduct extensive community consultation.
risks.evidence: refugees in settlements currently do not pay for water, the UNHCR and OPM are collaborating with the MWE on designing a new water tariff policy

risks.description: Over-reliance on diesel-powered mechanized pumping schemes exposes water schemes to high fuel costs, volatile operational expenses, and frequent service interruptions.
risks.mitigation: Prioritize solar-powered piped water systems and gravity-fed schemes during project design to minimize diesel reliance and lower running costs.
risks.evidence: long-term savings on fuel and capital maintenance make solar pumping systems more cost-effective than alternative mechanized pumping systems.

risks.description: Turnover of qualified financial management and procurement staff within MWE and NWSC could impair institutional memory and slow project implementation.
risks.mitigation: Maintain competitive staffing conditions, recruit dedicated PST specialists, and conduct regular hand-holding training sessions.
risks.evidence: turnover of qualified and experienced staff is noticed.
